s1.syndrome_frame: Congenital cerebral and ocular anomalies with prenatal and postnatal findings
salient_findings: Severe thinning of the frontal, parietal, and occipital lobes
key_facts: Born at 35 weeks 4 days’ gestation
Weight at birth: 2152 g
One of monochorionic diamniotic twins
Identical twin died in utero at 24 weeks
Fetal ultrasound showed microcephaly and ventricular enlargement
Postnatal MRI revealed microcephaly and marked enlargement of both lateral ventricles
No intracranial hematoma or neoplastic lesions
Family history was noncontributory
Weak light reflexes bilaterally at 1 week of age
Mild optic nerve pallor with suspected peripapillary double-ring sign

raw.syndrome_frame: Congenital cerebral and ocular anomalies with prenatal and postnatal findings
salient_findings: Severe thinning of the frontal, parietal, and occipital lobes
key_facts: Born at 35 weeks 4 days’ gestation
Weight at birth: 2152 g
One of monochorionic diamniotic twins
Identical twin died in utero at 24 weeks
Fetal ultrasound showed microcephaly and ventricular enlargement
Postnatal MRI revealed microcephaly and marked enlargement of both lateral ventricles
No intracranial hematoma or neoplastic lesions
Family history was noncontributory
Weak light reflexes bilaterally at 1 week of age
Mild optic nerve pallor with suspected peripapillary double-ring sign

shortlist.label: Walker-Warburg syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Characterized by congenital muscular dystrophy, ocular anomalies, and brain malformations, matching the patient's microcephaly, ventricular enlargement, and optic nerve pallor.

shortlist.label: Muscle-eye-brain disease
shortlist.why_kept: Presents with congenital muscular dystrophy, eye abnormalities, and brain malformations, consistent with the patient's findings of microcephaly, weak light reflexes, and suspected peripapillary double-ring sign.

shortlist.label: Fukuyama congenital muscular dystrophy
shortlist.why_kept: Involves congenital muscular dystrophy, brain malformations, and occasionally ocular anomalies, aligning with the patient's microcephaly, ventricular enlargement, and muscular dystrophy-like symptoms.

shortlist.label: Lissencephaly
shortlist.why_kept: Characterized by a smooth brain surface due to defective neuronal migration, which could explain the patient's microcephaly and ventricular enlargement.

shortlist.label: Cobblestone lissencephaly
shortlist.why_kept: Presents with a disorganized brain surface and ocular anomalies, consistent with the patient's microcephaly, ventricular enlargement, and optic nerve pallor.

shortlist.label: Aicardi syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Involves brain malformations, ocular anomalies, and sometimes muscular dystrophy-like symptoms, aligning with the patient's findings of microcephaly, weak light reflexes, and suspected peripapillary double-ring sign.

shortlist.label: Dandy-Walker malformation
shortlist.why_kept: Characterized by cerebellar hypoplasia and ventricular enlargement, which could explain the patient's marked enlargement of both lateral ventricles.

shortlist.label: Septo-optic dysplasia
shortlist.why_kept: Presents with optic nerve hypoplasia and sometimes brain malformations, consistent with the patient's mild optic nerve pallor and microcephaly.

raw.rationale: The combination of microcephaly, ventricular enlargement, and severe thinning of the frontal, parietal, and occipital lobes with preservation of the temporal lobes, basal ganglia, thalamus, brain stem, and cerebellum, along with the ocular findings of weak light reflexes and mild optic nerve pallor, is consistent with cobblestone lissencephaly, particularly in the context of a monochorionic diamniotic twin pregnancy with in utero death of the co-twin.

rejected.label: Walker-Warburg syndrome
rejected.why: While similar to cobblestone lissencephaly, Walker-Warburg syndrome typically presents with more severe ocular malformations, including cataracts and retinal detachment, which were not noted in this case.

rejected.label: Muscle-eye-brain disease
rejected.why: This condition typically presents with more pronounced muscular dystrophy and eye abnormalities, including glaucoma and retinal dysplasia, which were not described in this case.

rejected.label: Fukuyama congenital muscular dystrophy
rejected.why: This condition is characterized by significant muscular dystrophy and typically lacks the severe ocular and cerebral malformations seen in this case.

rejected.label: Lissencephaly
rejected.why: While lissencephaly is characterized by a smooth brain, it does not typically present with the cobblestone appearance and ocular findings seen in this case.

rejected.label: Aicardi syndrome
rejected.why: Aicardi syndrome typically presents with agenesis of the corpus callosum, chorioretinal lacunae, and other ocular abnormalities not described in this case.

rejected.label: Dandy-Walker malformation
rejected.why: Dandy-Walker malformation is characterized by hypoplasia of the cerebellar vermis and cystic dilation of the fourth ventricle, which were not noted in this case.

rejected.label: Septo-optic dysplasia
rejected.why: Septo-optic dysplasia typically presents with optic nerve hypoplasia, pituitary abnormalities, and midline brain defects, which were not described in this case.
